correctness.rationale: For uniform-parent rooted recursive trees let F_(n,r)=∑_v binom(L_v,r) for the number L_v of terminal children. Conditioned on the tree, increment drift is [F_(n,r-1)-r F_(n,r)]/n (F_0=n), because adding the new leaf increases its chosen parent's binomial count while a previously terminal chosen parent ceases to be a terminal child. This gives E F_(n,r)=n/(r+1)! for n≥r+1. For X=F_1, Y=F_2, Z=F_3, exact conditional increments are E∆X=1-X/n, E∆Y=(X-2Y)/n, E(∆X∆Y)=X/n, E(∆Y)^2=(X+4Y+6Z)/n. Product recurrence and true small n initial conditions give E X=n/2, E Y=n/6, E X²=n²/4+n/12, E XY=n²/12+n/8, E Y²=n²/36+59n/180. Thus for n≥5 Cov=n[[1/12,1/8],[1/8,59/180]], determinant 101n²/8640 and correlation 3sqrt(15)/(2sqrt59). Independently enumerated complete labeled parent-choice sets n≤8 and checked moments; induction proves general n. Rooted terminal children differ from unrooted graph-degree-one leaves.

Earlier recursive-tree fringe-motif covariance theory could potentially subsume when represented as an additive pattern mixture but no same statement or direct theorem implication was identified; any existing mean hierarchy is credited.
